name: modprobe
description: Loads or removes kernel modules (drivers, filesystems) with automatic dependency resolution.

flags.description: Load the module and its dependencies.
Remove the module (if not in use).
Load with parameters, e.g. modprobe snd_hda_intel model=generic.

examples.explanation: Loads the VirtualBox kernel driver on demand.
Unloads the USB storage driver (e.g. before a forensic image).
Verifies the module loaded and shows its dependents.
Prevents a module from loading at boot — the standard way to keep the nouveau driver away from NVIDIA systems.

about: Modules live in /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/. modprobe reads /etc/modprobe.d/ for options and blacklists and resolves dependencies automatically — unlike the raw insmod/rmmod, which require exact paths and ignore dependencies. Loaded modules appear in lsmod.
mistakes: Using insmod directly and failing on dependencies — modprobe handles them.
Expecting modprobe to persist across reboots — persistent loading needs /etc/modules-load.d/ entries.
warnings: Removing a module in use (check lsmod's Used by column) can destabilize the system; the kernel refuses when the count is nonzero.
